attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post, attributed to him and endorsed.

semantics.note: Observation is the right kind. But the drafter adds 'as originally introduced', which is not in the source. Marcus refers to the version that existed when he signed the petition a few days before the post, and the contract correctly treats that as the March 24 pre-replacement version. The drafter's added condition narrows the claim to the wrong version.

contract.note: Plain reading is fair and ordinary: 'stand in the way' means enactment would create a material legal obstacle to OpenAI's proposed restructuring, judged against the pre-replacement version. The contract fixes the drafter's version error.

evidence.note: Independent KQED report (April 10, 2025) says AB 501 would have blocked the conversion before it was changed to cover aircraft liens. Supports the claim in direction, but it is the reporter's description, not the bill text or a coverage analysis.
OpenAI's own disclosure of its nonprofit-controlled structure and the planned public benefit corporation. Explains what the restructuring was, but says nothing about how AB-501 would apply.
Legislative history listing a March 24 amendment and an April 3 amendment. Confirms the order of versions but contains no bill provisions.

reviews.rationale: The contract requires comparing the pre-replacement bill's operative provisions and coverage definitions with OpenAI's structure, and it treats reporting only as corroboration. The legislative text could not be retrieved. The only support is KQED's one-sentence description, and nothing in the packet shows the bill's restrictions or that they covered OpenAI. The evidence points toward support, but the packet does not meet the support condition.
